title: Scaling up successfully: Lessons from Kenya’s Tusome national literacy program
extended_summary:
This paper examines how Kenya’s Tusome national early grade literacy program was implemented at scale and whether the education system had the capacity to support the program’s instructional changes. The authors frame the study around a systems-oriented question: whether Tusome strengthened three core functions of an education system—setting expectations, monitoring progress/accountability, and providing differentiated support to schools and teachers.

Tusome built on prior pilot work, especially the PRIMR initiative, and was designed to deliver structured literacy instruction through teachers’ guides, student books, teacher training, and ongoing coaching. The program was implemented nationally in Kenyan public primary schools and low-cost private APBET schools, with curriculum support officers (CSOs) or instructional coaches visiting classrooms, observing lessons, and providing feedback. The paper draws on program documents, training materials, dashboard data, internal monitoring information, and an external evaluation of learning outcomes.

The authors conclude that Tusome succeeded in clarifying benchmark expectations, increasing classroom visits and feedback, and creating functional monitoring systems through government structures. Basic instructional inputs were widely available, and student learning gains were large on both Kiswahili and English assessments. However, the program did not fully use classroom observation data to target support to the teachers and schools that needed it most. Overall, the paper argues that coherent, structured pedagogy plus frequent coaching and monitoring can support large-scale instructional reform, but differentiated intervention based on data remained underdeveloped.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed implementation/scale-up case study using program documents, monitoring data, and an external evaluation, but it is not itself a randomized or quasi-experimental impact study. The paper’s methodology is primarily descriptive and qualitative with some secondary quantitative reporting, so it meets limited credibility criteria.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported learning gains are large for K-12 interventions, with effect sizes ranging from 0.63 to 1.04 SD on early grade reading outcomes and substantial benchmark increases. The intervention also shows strong system-level improvements in monitoring, accountability, and instructional support at national scale.

finding.finding_summary: This paper evaluates Kenya’s national Tusome literacy scale-up and finds that the program strengthened system capacity for setting expectations, monitoring performance, and delivering instructional support through government structures. The study reports large gains in learning outcomes as well: external evaluation results showed average effect sizes of 0.63 SD in Class 1 and 0.76 SD in Class 2 for Kiswahili, and 0.67 SD in Class 1 and 1.04 SD in Class 2 for English, alongside improved benchmark attainment from 34% to 65% in English and 37% to 66% in Kiswahili for Class 2 students.
finding.measure: System capacity indicators (expectations, monitoring, support), classroom visit counts, dashboard/accountability use, and external evaluation reading outcomes/benchmark attainment
finding.study_size: national_scale; external evaluation sample size not_reported
finding.effect_size: 0.63 SD (Kiswahili Class 1 avg), 0.76 SD (Kiswahili Class 2 avg), 0.67 SD (English Class 1 avg), 1.04 SD (English Class 2 avg)

finding.finding_summary: Tusome produced large and statistically significant improvements in early grade reading outcomes in both Kiswahili and English. In Kiswahili, all six subtasks improved with average effect sizes of 0.63 SD (Class 1) and 0.76 SD (Class 2); in English, all eight subtasks improved with average effect sizes of 0.67 SD (Class 1) and 1.04 SD (Class 2).
finding.measure: EGRA-style reading subtasks: letter sounds, syllable fluency, invented/nonword decoding, oral reading fluency, reading comprehension, listening comprehension, phoneme segmentation, vocabulary
finding.study_size: national_scale; external evaluation sample size not_reported
